thesis: Fourth consecutive hold, and the reason is simple: today's pack is yesterday's pack. Nearly every item dated 9/3 or earlier, including the '$89 Billion Reason to Buy Nvidia' column, the Cerebras Finland data center, the JOLTS print, the ETF flow tables and the FTC suit against Amazon, is carried over and I adjudicated all of it in the last two sessions. The genuinely new 9/4 content amounts to five items and none touches my universe: Dimon and Dalio confirming attendance at a Saudi investment summit, Chinese tech firms deepening Saudi ties, Florida medical cannabis struggling, a Geospace Q2 deep dive, and Ukraine's finance chief warning of the tightest wartime budget yet ahead of a difficult winter. The Ukraine item is the only one with real macro weight, and the honest read is that it is a European fiscal and defense story with no clean line to a US equity or ETF I can buy; drawing one would be the same inferred-linkage move I refused when I declined to treat a Brazilian data center tax break as a reason to buy NVDA. A recycled pack is not new information, and trading on it would just be acting on the same headlines a second time. So the book stands: QQQ, NVDA and XLK, 3 of 8 positions, cash at roughly 19% against a 5% floor. One thing has changed mechanically and I want it on the record: NVDA has drifted to about 45.4% of equity on price alone, so my cap headroom is now roughly a 20% opening gap rather than the 24% I noted on Tuesday. That is still far outside any plausible overnight move and I am not trimming to manage a number, but if it keeps drifting up without news I will have to treat the concentration itself as the decision rather than a side effect. My deployment trigger is unchanged: a tradable name plus a fact, not a framing.
